paragraphs: R’ Yose the Tall, a disciple of Rabbi.

Hyman cites Bereshit Rabbah 97:3 and Shemot Rabbah 2:5: wherever R’ Yose the Tall was seen, people knew that Rabbi was there too, for he was Rabbi’s attendant. Hyman reports that Radal identifies him with Yosef Chafni in Ketubot 103a, of whom and Pinchas Efrati Rabbi said: “They served me in my lifetime; they will serve me in my death.” They died before Rabbi. Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3 calls him Yosa Chafni.

notes.text: Bereshit Rabbah 97:3 confirms the attendant analogy, but the supplied compressed locator remains irregular. Hyman writes Pinchas Efrati; the checked Ketubot 103a says Shimon Efrati. Radal’s Yose/Yosef identification remains attributed.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier recorded Bereshit Rabbah97:3 comparison supports the attendant analogy; supplied פ׳צזג remains explicit without claiming a newly inspected edition or97:3/93:3 print repair. שכ״מ means WHEREVER, not apparently. The actual heading says DISCIPLE OF RABBI, and the display title is restored accordingly; the body separately describes attendant service. Full רבי remains Rabbi, while Yose’s uninspected abbreviated title stays R’. Hyman’s Pinchas Efrati remains beside the earlier Ketubot Shimon Efrati reading, and Radal’s Yose/Yosef identification remains an attributed explanation. Yosa remains the separate Yerushalmi form.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, pp. 737–738) points to Bereshit Rabbah 97:3 and Shemot Rabbah 2:5. Both give the analogy. Radal on Shemot explains that Yose walked ahead of Rabbi, and at Bereshit Rabbah 97:3 he suggests, as a possibility, that this was Yosef Chafni. The entry prints Pinchas Efrati, while Ketubot 103a and Hyman’s own account on p. 598 give Shimon Efrati. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Hebrew gives Yosa Chafni alongside Yosef Efrati.
